maya: Follow-up from the postmortem for the KV-cache eviction recurrence (see postmortem link in doc). We agreed we need exact triage steps, verified mitigation commands, and a clarified escalation ladder. Please claim specific pieces + ETA.
maya: Also want a durable detector (alert) for the recurring pattern and a quarterly runbook drill to validate mitigation.
rachel: I'll own the runbook checklist and canonical commands. ETA: 2026-04-01. I'll write expected success/failure outputs to reduce ambiguity.
omar: I'll wire the alert and ticket automation. Proposal: alert when eviction_signature_count >= 3 in 24h OR inference_service.p99_delta > 180ms for 10m. Will send draft alert rules. ETA: 2026-03-30.
jun: I'll coordinate the sprint slot and run the staging simulation. I'll allocate 1.5 dev-days next sprint.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-8000 and linked to postmortem: https://tickets.redwood/INF-8000 (runbook + alert + drill).
rachel: Draft triage checklist (to add to runbook):
1) Confirm logs include the eviction signature: `grep -i "KVCache eviction" /var/log/runtime/*.log`
2) Verify cache metrics: `curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_entries` -> expect drop after eviction
3) Identify affected pod: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'`
4) Run safe-evict in staging: `kubectl -n inference exec -it $POD -- /bin/sh -c "curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9090/debug/cache/evict"`
5) Post-evict smoke: monitor 5m for 5xx spike >0.5% or CPU >85% and rollback if seen.
rachel: Expected outputs: the evict endpoint returns `\{"status\":\"ok\"\}` and `kv_cache_entries` metric should drop by >10%. Add these asserts to the runbook.
omar: Alert draft (Datadog/Prometheus pseudo-syntax):
- name: KVCacheEvictionPattern
- condition: sum(last_24h:eviction_signature{service:inference}) >= 3 OR increase(inference_service_p99_ms[10m]) > 180
- action: create ticket INF-8000 and page #infra-oncall via PagerDuty routing.
omar: Will add an automated play that adds `postmortem-followup` tag to tickets created by this alert.
jun: For the staging drill I propose: run the evict endpoint on staging cluster, run through recovery checklist, validate no user-facing errors, and time to recover. I'll schedule the drill for 2026-04-08 and create a calendar invite for participants.
carla: I'll review the runbook wording to ensure SREs can follow it during noisy incidents. Also suggest a short troubleshooting FAQ section: "If evict returns 500, capture core dumps and rollback cache process restart."
ops-bot: INF-8000 updated: subtask INF-8000-1 (runbook edits) assigned to rachel; INF-8000-2 (alert wiring) assigned to omar; INF-8000-3 (drill + validation) assigned to jun. Links: https://tickets.redwood/INF-8000
rachel: Pasted commands into a PR draft: https://git.redwood/runbooks/pull/510. Added expected outputs + rollback criteria.
jun: I validated the staging flow this morning: evict endpoint returned {"status":"ok"}, metrics showed kv_cache_entries drop ~12%, no 5xx increase. Left validation notes in the PR.
omar: Alert wired to Datadog and test alert created (did a test ticket). The automation adds tag `auto-created-by-alert` and pages infra. Posting alert rule in INF-8000.
rachel: PR merged: https://git.redwood/runbooks/commit/e5c2f1  runbook updated with triage checklist, commands, asserts, and rollback guidance.
maya: Great work. Jun, confirm drill invite + attendees and paste the post-drill notes in INF-8000. Omar, after alert is live, please run a 1-week observation and report any false positives.
jun: Invite sent for 2026-04-08; attendees: rachel, omar, jun, carla, oncall lead. I'll post notes after drill.
omar: Alert live. Will monitor for 7 days and log any hits to INF-8000.
carla: Quick suggestion added to runbook: add a pointer to the metric dashboard and a playbook snippet for incremental mitigation (throttle background jobs to reduce cache pressure).
maya: Closing loop here once INF-8000 shows: runbook merged, alert observed for 7d, drill completed with green validation. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
